summary: Panel filter propagation ordering causes inconsistent SLO counts across dashboard and SLO card
description:
Issue summary: After the v2.17.1 console rollout we are seeing cases where dashboard panels and the SLO card return different counts for the same route and time range when a sequence of panel-level filters and dashboard variables are applied.

Impact: FluxDrive (dedicated) is seeing alerts silence or fail to fire because the SLO card count (used by their alerting rule) reports a lower event count than the dashboard panels. This is causing missed PagerDuty notifications and customer confusion. Approx 3% of queries for the affected org in us-west are misattributed during certain filter permutations.

Environment: prod (us-west), Redwood Console v2.17.1, SLO service v1.8.3. Customer has a dedicated capacity pool and custom route tags.

Observed behavior:
- Apply dashboard variables: environment=production, route_prefix=/api/v2, client_id=fluxdrive
- In a panel add additional filters: has_tracehook=true and tag:release in [stable,canary]
- Panel A (timeseries) shows 12,432 events for 24h; SLO card (same dashboard, same time bounds, same variables) shows 11,987 events.
- Reordering filters (moving tag:release to a higher precedence) causes the SLO card to flip to match the panel counts for a short period, then diverge on subsequent refreshes.

Expected behavior: Dashboard panels and the SLO card should run the same underlying query (or compatible aggregations) with identical filter propagation semantics and return consistent counts within sampling tolerance.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Login as organization admin for FluxDrive in prod (us-west)
2) Open dashboard 'Customer API — Uptime & SLOs' (id: 8142 in FluxDrive org)
3) Set global dashboard variables: timespan=24h, environment=production, route_prefix=/api/v2
4) On panel 'Request volume' add ad-hoc filters: has_tracehook=true AND tag:release IN (stable,canary)
5) Observe counts in panel and compare to SLO card at top-right; toggle filter order and refresh repeatedly
6) Capture network traces and console logs when divergence occurs

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: filter application ordering regression in the async filter propagator introduced in v2.17.1; frontend sometimes sends variable deltas out-of-order which the query-engine reorders differently for SLO card vs panels.
Reproduced on internal staging with a FluxDrive snapshot when we replay the dashboard variable change traffic and simulate network latency between frontend and the propagation service.

Observed that the SLO card request was batched into an aggregate evaluation job (slo-evaluator) that applies canonical filter normalization. Panels use the ad-hoc query path which can receive out-of-order filter updates causing a different WHERE clause ordering and a different planner path (index vs seq scan) leading to subtle sampling differences.

Tracehook interaction: panels with has_tracehook=true add an additional join that amplifies ordering differences; changing filter precedence can change join-join ordering and therefore the join algorithm chosen by the query-engine.
Relevant rollout: console v2.17.1 introduced 'async-propagator' (PR #8420) to reduce UI jank; rollback of that component on staging makes counts consistent again.
Metric offsets: discrepancy magnitude correlates with sampling windows when the query-engine selects a sampled fast-path; non-sampled execution returns identical counts.
Potentially related issues: SUP-11723 (SLO percentile dimension loss after retention) — included because both involve SLO evaluation and filter normalization changes.
comments: 2026-03-08 10:05 - Aisha Patel (Support): Reached out to FluxDrive CSM (Jordan Meyers) for example dashboard id and timeslices. Provided temporary workaround: toggle 'Use canonical query mode' on SLO card settings. Waiting for customer to confirm impact.

2026-03-09 14:22 - Marco Li (Eng): Reproduced locally with replay tool. Confirmed async-propagator reorder bug when variable-change events arrive with >250ms gap. Patch candidate prepared to serialize variable deltas per-dashboard (branch: fix/serialize-propagator-305246).

2026-03-10 09:18 - Daniel Park (SRE): Deployed a canary of the propagator-serialize patch to staging and ran FluxDrive snapshot load. Counts aligned across panels and SLO card after canary. No CPU/RAM regression observed.

2026-03-11 11:02 - Aisha Patel (Support): Customer verified that enabling canonical query mode reduced missed alerts but complains about slightly increased SLO evaluation latency. Customer asks for timeline for full fix in prod.

2026-03-12 17:45 - Marco Li (Eng): Planning rollout: bake patch on prod with 10% orgs ring for 48h, then 50% for 24h. Post-rollout monitoring dashboard created (id: 9102) to track panel vs slo_card divergence metric.
next_steps: 1) Merge and CI the serializer patch (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/8420) and coordinate prod rollout with SRE
2) Add e2e test that replays variable-change events with jitter to catch reorder regressions
3) Document 'canonical query mode' behavior for customers as a temporary mitigation
4) Postmortem if rollout is needed across >200 orgs or if alerts continue to be missed after rollout
resolution: In Progress — workaround (enable canonical query mode) communicated to customer. Patch under code review; staged canary successful in staging. Waiting for SRE window to start prod ring on 2026-03-14.
resolution_notes: Workaround: toggle 'Use canonical query mode' on the SLO card to force normalization of filters (customer-facing temporary mitigation).
Fix: serialize variable delta propagation per-dashboard in async-propagator; ensures deterministic ordering for both panels and SLO evaluator.
